messages:
maya (support): Heads-up — customer ACME reports repeated 429s right after a ~25s traffic spike. They believe the ephemeral quota cushion didn't refill quickly and requests got routed to a slower fallback, causing latency spikes. Can we confirm how the cushion/refill and routing interact?

sam (eng-sre): thanks, Maya. can you paste the request pattern they saw? qps, payload size, and whether they were pinned to a model version?

maya (support): copy of customer note: \"~200 concurrent short completions (payload ~150 bytes) for ~25s, then dropped to idle. Immediately after, many requests got 429 or routed to t2-small fallback with +300ms tail latency. They expected the short-term buffer to cover the burst. Account: acme-01234\"

kevin (eng-runtime): ok. quick primer: ephemeral quota (we call it cushion) is refilled on a sliding 60s window but also gated by per-route reservation and priority tier. if a route triggers fallback routing due to capacity, some tokens may be consumed from the cushion then held until the refill tick. that can look like \"linger\".

maya (support): is that a bug or expected behavior? customer says it used to refill instantly in older tests.

sam (eng-sre): expected in some configs. TL;DR: refill is not per-request instant; it's aggregated. also, when autoscaler is spinning up new dedicated capacity, we prefer safe fallback routing instead of letting requests pile on. two things to confirm for ACME: 1) did they have per-route burst allowance enabled? 2) did they have priority > standard?

maya (support): they said standard priority, no special per-route burst flag enabled.

kevin (eng-runtime): steps to reproduce locally (use on-staging): run 200 concurrent requests for 20–30s, then stop and immediately issue a sustained low rate. example load command:

```
# simple load using hey
hey -n 20000 -c 200 -m POST -H \"Authorization: Bearer $STAGING_KEY\" -H \"X-Account-ID: acme-01234\" -d '{"input":"x"}' https://staging-infer.redwood.internal/v1/generate
```

This will show the cushion drain and the refill tick behavior in the logs.

sam (eng-sre): to collect helpful logs for us, run the same load and then paste these two snippets from the routing logs around the spike window: `route.decisions`, `quota.bucket.status`. also include the top-line `request.latency` histogram.

maya (support): got it. customer also asked if there's any short-term mitigation we can offer while you investigate.

kevin (eng-runtime): immediate mitigations: 1) temporarily raise the per-route cushion via console for ACME (we can do a small bump), 2) reduce concurrency from client side to smooth the spike, or 3) enable their higher priority tier for short window. none of these are ideal long-term but they stop 429s quickly.

maya (support): I can stage a 15% cushion bump and offer a client-side concurrency cap. want me to proceed?

sam (eng-sre): yes go ahead with the temporary cushion bump and ask them to run the repro command and send logs. I'll open an internal ticket to check if the refill tick logic is causing the observed 20–40s linger after short bursts. tagging @kevin to own runtime changes.

kevin (eng-runtime): thanks — if we confirm the refill aggregation is the culprit we can consider a smaller refill granularity or an adaptive refill for standard-tier routes. will post a follow-up in this thread after I have traces.

ops-bot: Incident created — INC-2026-0743 for \"ephemeral cushion linger after short spike\". assigned to eng-runtime.

maya (support): customer informed of temporary bump and repro steps. I'll paste their logs here once they send them. :thumbsup:
